 Print this Article 
 View Comments Revolution teammates swarm their captain, Carles Gil (10), after he struck home a 91st minute penalty that proved crucial in a 2-1 win over the Philadelphia Union back on Oct. 24 in Chester, Penn. Photo courtesy of New England Revolution FOXBOROUGH — With captain Carles Gil leading the way, the Revolution probably shouldn’t be in the midst of a five-year playoff victory drought. But when the Revolution play host to the Philadelphia Union Saturday (2 p.m.), they will be seeking their first postseason win since 2020. 
 Their track record might explain why they are the only home underdogs in the opening game of the MLS playoffs, despite finishing with the fourth-best record in the league. 
 History, and the oddsmakers, might be against the Revolution, but that’s not concerning coach Marko Mitrovic. 
 “This group has our own dynamic, our own history and record,” Mitrovic said Thursday. “So, what is in the past, we have massive respect toward that, but we have the present moment, and we are very focused on the present moment.” 
 Mitrovic has been able to, so far, blank out past failings, keep players motivated, and make the right tactical moves. Management has played a part, providing late-season roster reinforcements Daniel Gazdag and Jack Harrison in midfield, and Josh Wynder in defense. 
 The Revolution (18-12-4, 58 points) finished third in the Eastern Conference. But they lost their final two games, squandering a chance to overtake second-place Inter Miami. Proving costly were goals negated by offside in losses to Miami (2-1) and Orlando City SC (1-0), plus Mitrovic resting starters in the second half against Orlando City. But the decision to attempt to preserve health, plus a two-week layoff, might yet pay off. Gil and Peyton Miller have recovered from minor, undisclosed injuries, and Harrison (quadriceps) returns after a two-month absence. 
 Related : Why did Peyton Miller, the Revolution’s fast-rising star, turn down millions from the Premier League? Gil, 33, is the Revolution’s oldest starter, and his poise in possession is key to composed performances. He led the team in goals (career-high 13) and assists (13) for the third time in four years. 
 “We have a clear idea of what to do,” said Gil, who skipped practice Thursday and planned to return Friday. “When you are a team that has a clear identity and knows what to do in every moment, you feel very confident. 
 “We don’t have to change much. We need to maintain our sense of calmness. These types of games can be emotional. The emotions can sometimes make you do things that you normally would not do. You have to try to control those emotions. But we’re really calm. We know this is an important moment that’s coming, but we need to stay on the same path. We’ve trained well during the week. I think we’re ready for the match on Saturday.” 
 In 2019, Gil’s arrival, along with the hiring of Bruce Arena, signaled renewed hope as the Revolution reached the playoffs after a three-year absence. They defeated Orlando City, 3-1, before falling in the 2020 Eastern Conference final. But that would be it for postseason wins, as a record-setting 2021 Supporters’ Shield season concluded with a penalty-kicks loss to New York City FC, and the 2023 playoffs with a two-game elimination by the Union. 
 Related : Sullivan: Matt Turner’s return to the Revolution has been the key to a renaissance, for both the goalkeeper and his team This time, it will be a best-of-three series, with the Revolution holding home-field advantage. They might have gained another edge as the Union will be missing captain Andre Blake (groin), a former UConn goalkeeping star who was called in to Jamaica’s Nations League matches but did not play. Also in their favor could be Gazdag, who led the Union to a 7-1-1 record (the only defeat in the meaningless 2023 season-ender) as a starter against the Revolution from 2021-25, before joining the Columbus Crew. 
 Revolution coach Marko Mitrovic was beaming after his club's 2-1 win at the Union back on Oct. 24. Photo courtesy of New England Revolution The Revolution snapped a six-match losing streak against the Union this season, patiently staving off high-pressure defending, and scoring on late-game counterattacks in a pair of 2-1 victories. 
 “We just have to be who we are, and do what we do every day, without changing something now in our approach, or comparing it with what we have done so far this season,” Mitrovic said. “I’m very aware that it’s different, maybe you can say it’s higher stakes. But our approach is just the same. I think this team played with a high level of urgency from the very beginning. We kind of built that survival mode from the very beginning of the season. I don’t think that we had that luxury where we could kind of take a break and slow down in any given moment. 
 “I think when you come to those knockout-stage games, that’s what you have to do. You have no time to slow down, you have no time to not maximize every single action on the field. That’s what we are doing so far, and we’re going to keep doing the same things.”
